Further options of the wrappers

Source: R/presets.R
extremes_control.Rd

The wrappers keep their signatures short; the less common options go in a control list, in the style of stats::glm.control().

Usage

extremes_control(
  exclude_below = NULL,
  yearly = FALSE,
  spell_excess = FALSE,
  min_coverage = 0.8,
  fill_missing = FALSE,
  keep_steps = FALSE,
  dry_run = FALSE,
  chunk = "auto",
  verbose = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

indices_control(
  min_coverage = 0.8,
  fill_missing = FALSE,
  keep_steps = FALSE,
  dry_run = FALSE,
  chunk = "auto",
  verbose = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  .parallel = FALSE
)

controls_control(
  fill_missing = TRUE,
  keep_steps = FALSE,
  dry_run = FALSE,
  verbose = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

Arguments

exclude_below

Values left out of percentiles, e.g. 0.1 mm for wet days. For precipitation percentiles it defaults to 0.1.

yearly

Also compute year-round percentiles.

spell_excess

Also compute spell-length percentiles and the excess of each spell over them, when percentiles are used.

min_coverage

Share of a window that must be covered by data.

fill_missing

Fill missing cells from their neighbours before extracting.

keep_steps

Return a list with every intermediate table instead of the final one.

dry_run

Print the plan and the estimated sizes, and stop.

chunk

Splitting of large steps, passed to the steps; see ?c4e.

verbose

FALSE silences messages and progress.

label

Name shown in progress messages.

.parallel

Fit SPI/SPEI series with furrr.

Value

A list of class c4e_control.

See also

weather_extremes(), climate_indices(), static_controls(), time_varying_controls()

Examples

extremes_control(min_coverage = 1, keep_steps = TRUE)
#> $exclude_below
#> NULL
#> 
#> $yearly
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $spell_excess
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $min_coverage
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $fill_missing
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $keep_steps
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $dry_run
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $chunk
#> [1] "auto"
#> 
#> $verbose
#> NULL
#> 
#> $label
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "c4e_control"
